Create Performance Task

The Create PT is 30% of your AP score and the most controllable 30 points in the building. You get 9 hours of class time (Apr 13-27 for us) to build an individual program, and you submit three things to the AP Digital Portfolioby 2027-04-30, 11:59 PM ET. On the May exam you then answer written-response questions about this exact program — so build something you understand deeply, not something impressive you cannot explain.

The program requirements (all five, or it caps your score)

RequirementWhat it meansWhere you already did this
List(s)At least one list that stores data your program uses — not just for showCard jam deck: List<Card_data>; boss phases; waypoint arrays
Procedure with a parameterA student-developed procedure (method) that takes at least one parameterChangeHealth(int amount), Shuffle(List<Card_data> deck)
Algorithm: sequencing + selection + iterationInside that procedure: statements in order, an if/else, and a loopEnemy state machine; deck traversal with conditionals
Call to the procedureSomething in your program actually calls itEverywhere — you call your own code
Input and outputThe program takes input (buttons, clicks, keys) and produces output (screen, audio, motion)Every game you have built since September
Trap: the "impressive" program. Graders cannot give points for ambition you cannot explain. A card game, a grid puzzle, a small boss fight, a 2-button toy — all of these earn 6/6 when you can walk through every line. Pick something you can finish and fully understand, not a physics-based MMO.

What you submit (3 pieces)

  • Program code — your whole program, as a PDF or a file upload, including the list, the procedure, and the call.
  • Video — under 60 seconds, showing the program running: input, then the behavior it causes. Plan it like a jam demo; screen-record it in one take.
  • Personalized Project Reference (PPR) — screen captures of (1) your list, (2) your procedure with its parameter, and (3) the algorithm inside it. The PPR is the ONLY thing you see during the exam's written-response section — make it legible and complete.

The collaboration line (read this twice)

You MAY: brainstorm together, look at each other's code, pair-debug, reuse ideas from our starter project and the internet (with attribution in comments — you learned this in9.10a).

You may NOT: submit code you did not personally write for this task, share your PPR, or let anyone write your video's program. The College Board treats unattributed copying as an integrity violation that can void the whole exam.

The deadline is real. 2027-04-30, 11:59 PM ET is a national deadline — no extensions, no late work, no "my laptop died." We submit in class on Apr 29 so a bad evening never costs you 30%.
